description: The HGVS recommendations' own worked normalization examples — rows where the spec names an input and prints, in the same sentence, what the description must be instead. Two rules are covered: the coding-sequence restriction on repeat notation (repeat units must be a multiple of 3, with the UTRs carved out) and the 3'rule's exon/exon-junction exception. Both are sequence-dependent, so neither can fire in the harvested spec fixture, which normalizes through an empty MockProvider. Here they run against real reference bases served from the committed hermetic slice beside this file. Each row is pinned under all three shipped input-hygiene modes, because they do not agree and which mode produces which answer is itself the finding.

cases.note: A 1-nt repeat unit on a coding reference: not a multiple of 3, so the repeat spelling is unavailable and the spec prints the dup form to use instead. Ferro converts it, in every mode.

A 2-nt repeat unit on a coding reference: same restriction, and the spec prints the insertion form to use instead. STRICT MODE REJECTS THE SPEC'S OWN INPUT: the reference tract at c.1738 is not a whole number of TA copies ('expected TA[k] (k whole copies), found T (1 bp; unit_len 2 does not divide span)'), so a mode that refuses to repair a reference mismatch cannot reach the prescribed answer. Recorded as observed behaviour, not endorsed — nobody has adjudicated whether strict mode should accept an input the spec publishes.
The other half of the same sentence: the prescribed form is itself a fixed point. Without this row a normalizer that rewrote the answer into some third spelling would still satisfy the row above.
Fixed-point half of the insertion row — and note it is accepted in strict mode, unlike the repeat spelling of the same variant.

citation.quote: As such, `NM_024312.4:c.-6_-3G[6]` is valid as the reading frame is not affected.

cases.note: The carve-out, and the row that makes the two above meaningful: the restriction is scoped to the coding sequence, so a 1-nt repeat unit in the 5'UTR keeps its repeat spelling. A normalizer that simply refused all short repeat units on a `c.` reference would pass the CDS rows and fail here.
The RNA axis carries the same restriction, stated separately in RNA/repeated.md.
RNA counterpart of the 2-nt unit row, and it inherits the same strict-mode rejection — the tract it names is the same one.
Fixed-point half of the RNA dup row.
Fixed-point half of the RNA insertion row.

citation.quote: the format r.-125_-123cug[4] should not be used; it contains redundant information

cases.note:
THE SPEC SELF-CONFLICT ROW. `RNA/repeated.md:22` marks range-plus-unit invalid as redundant — the range `-125_-123` already fixes the unit — while `:27` publishes `NM_024312.4:r.-6_-3g[6]`, exactly that shape, as valid. The two cannot both hold. Ferro still answers in two ways by input-hygiene mode: the plain library path leaves the published form alone, strict rejects the input outright. Recorded as the ruling `rna-repeat-range-plus-unit-redundancy` in tests/fixtures/grammar/hgvs_spec_normalization_overrides.json, and owed upstream via #466.

LENIENT MOVED IN #1631, and it moved ONTO the spec's published string — this row was the recorded divergence and no longer is. The W3013 repair used to drop the repeat UNIT and keep the RANGE, emitting `r.-6_-3[6]`; by `:20` a bare range denotes one unit whose length is the range's length, so that was a four-nucleotide unit six times (24 nt) where the input is a single `g` six times (6 nt) — a different variant, silently. The repair now keeps the unit and reduces the range to its anchor, giving the normalizer `r.-6g[6]`.

WHAT PUTS THE RANGE BACK IS THE NORMALIZER, NOT THE REPAIR, and that is the part worth not misreading. `NM_024312.4` carries `gggg` at `r.-6` to `r.-3`, so `normalize_repeat`'s tract maximization widens the anchor to the maximal `g` tract and re-emits `r.-6_-3g[6]` — the input, and `:27`'s form. So the lenient answer agrees with `:27` while `:22` calls the string it agrees on invalid; agreement here is not a conformance verdict. That re-widening is the #1618 family (what a copy count is counted against) on the RNA axis, and it is pinned separately by `the_lenient_repair_hands_the_normalizer_the_anchored_form` in tests/it/issue_1631_repeat_label_repair.rs.

citation.quote: the variant is described as `LRG_199t1:c.3921dup` (`NC_000023.10:g.32459297dup`) and not as `c.3922dup`

cases.note: The flagship worked example of the 3'rule's exon-junction exception (`general.md:43`), and the direction the exception is normally tested: c.3920=A, c.3921=T, c.3922=T, so the unrestricted 3'rule would shift this dup across the junction into the next exon. It must not, and does not. See the sibling row for the direction that is NOT asserted.

citation.quote: the variant (`NC_000023.11:g.32441180dup`) is **not described** as `c.3922dup` since this would shift the position of the variant to the next exon

cases.note: CONVERGENCE, as decided — the row that MOVED when #1621 landed. c.3921 and c.3922 are both T, so at the transcript level `c.3921dup` and `c.3922dup` denote one sequence; ferro nonetheless emitted two fixed points, projecting 2,790 bp apart (`LRG_199:g.903430dup` vs `g.906220dup`, matching the spec's own `g.32459297dup` vs `g.32456507dup`). `spec_expected` was null until the `exon-junction-dup-converge-from-the-far-side` ruling found the spec answering this input three times independently: `duplication.md:26` names c.3921dup as THE description and says the variant is not described as c.3922dup, `:60` restates that on the GRCh38 coordinates, and `:148` gives the reason — translating c.3922dup back to a genomic position lands at the wrong nucleotide, in the wrong exon. The 3'rule's exon-junction clamp now binds from BOTH sides, so all three modes emit the spec's answer and this row is no longer a divergence. The sibling `c.3921dup` row did not move; keeping both is what distinguishes 'the clamp binds from either side' from 'everything drifts 5''.
